question: In neonatal resuscitation, positive pressure ventilation (PPV) should be initiated when the heart rate is below 100 bpm after completing the initial stabilisation steps within the golden minute.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The statement is TRUE. PPV is indicated when HR <100 bpm or when breathing is absent or ineffective after completing initial stabilisation steps. 60 bpm is the threshold for adding chest compressions — a different, later decision point. These two thresholds (60 and 100 bpm) must not be confused.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! Per NRP/HBB, PPV is initiated when HR <100 bpm (or if breathing is absent/inadequate) after the initial steps — drying, stimulation, warmth, airway positioning — are completed within the first 60 seconds (the golden minute). The rate threshold is 100 bpm, not 60 bpm (which is the threshold to add chest compressions).
